title: Record ownership
summary: Check who owns a record after checking permission to call its endpoint.

richText: A role controls access to a kind of operation. It does not tell Spring who owns a database record.
Two users can both have USER and still have different journal entries.
authenticated() lets either user reach the endpoint. Your application must still check that the requested entry belongs to the current user.
Read the owner ID from the authenticated account. Do not accept the caller’s user ID as proof of ownership.
Query by both entry ID and owner ID, or compare the stored owner before using the record.
Apply this check when reading, updating and deleting records.
Use an immutable account ID when usernames can change.
An ownership failure may return 404 to avoid revealing whether another user’s record exists. Use this policy consistently.
